defects.what: This new test file is outside the brief's allowed files (the script plus quoted titles only), and the brief said any other change meant stopping and reporting why. The test is useful: before this change no test ran check_doc_links.py, even though docs/testing.md implied the suite caught broken links. It still breaks the brief's file list.
This prose edit is outside the allowed files. It is not a citation-title fix: it adds a sentence about the new test file.
The paragraph was not reflowed after the insertion, so this line is 91 characters, past the doc's ~76-column width.
The reflow is only partial: it leaves a short ragged line, 'is not built. Nothing here would change', in the middle of the paragraph.

structured_output.summary: `title_ok` now requires `t in heads`, a whole match after `norm()`, once a title is known to be a section reference. The `t in text` fallback is unchanged. I checked completeness by running the base tree with the whole-heading rule. Exactly five citations relied on the prefix: architecture.md:158, design-system.md:366, frontend-pages.md:474, frontend.md:317 and llm.md:402. All five now quote the full heading, and no heading was renamed. The checker reports 0 misses, ruff is clean and pytest passes. The module docstring was updated and is accurate. The new tests pin the rule: one fails when the script is reverted. They also test the cross-doc case and the text fallback. The weak point is scope. The change adds tests/test_doc_links.py and a sentence in docs/testing.md, and neither file is on the brief's allowed list. That edit also leaves one line in testing.md over width, and llm.md's partial reflow leaves a ragged line. The design-system.md citation drops a redundant `components/ui/` because the full heading now contains it, which is justified. I didn't count the out-of-scope test as lines to fix, because it closes a real coverage gap a reviewer would likely keep.
